summary: React + Tailwind SPA Valentine proposal site. User now requires a newly generated cartoon kitty illustration based on a provided reference (not inserting an external photo), a more classy/aesthetic background, and refined “No” interactions: the No button must persist (especially on mobile), evade on proximity, and each No click spawns a random teasing message that appears at random positions and can animate/move around; the No label should return after showing teasing text above/near the moving button. “Yes” still triggers a Yayyyy success screen with fireworks.

existing_features.title: Valentine proposal screen with primary kitty illustration
existing_features.description: Renders the main proposal prompt (“Victoria will you be my valentine ?”) with a centered layout, romantic gradient background, and a primary illustration loaded from a public static asset (/assets/generated/proposal-kitty.jpeg).

existing_features.title: Proximity-based evasive “No” button
existing_features.description: Tracks mouse movement and, when the cursor comes within a proximity threshold of the No button, repositions the button to a new random location while constraining it within the main centered container bounds.

existing_features.title: Cycling teasing label on the “No” button
existing_features.description: Each No click increments a counter that cycles the No button label through multiple teasing phrases while keeping the main prompt text unchanged.

existing_features.title: Ephemeral teasing popups on “No” clicks
existing_features.description: On each No click, spawns a short-lived popup positioned near the No button using a fixed overlay element and a dedicated CSS animation; popups automatically expire and repeated clicks accumulate multiple independent popups.

existing_features.title: “Yes” acceptance success screen with fireworks and “Yayyyy!”
existing_features.description: Clicking Yes switches to a success state that displays a large “Yayyyy!” message, a success kitty image, and an animated fireworks celebration overlay.

existing_features.title: Fireworks particle celebration component
existing_features.description: Generates repeated bursts of colored particles at preset screen-relative positions using an interval; particles animate outward via CSS variables (angle/velocity) and are removed after a timeout.

existing_features.title: Floating hearts animated background with pattern overlay
existing_features.description: Creates randomized heart particles on mount and animates them upward across the viewport; also renders a faint repeating/cover background pattern image from /assets/generated/....

existing_features.title: Valentine-themed styling system (Tailwind + OKLCH tokens + custom animations)
existing_features.description: Defines a Valentine color palette and dark-mode overrides via CSS variables, extends Tailwind with Valentine color aliases and glow shadow, and provides custom keyframe animations (float-up, heart-beat, teasing-popup, firework-particle, etc.).

existing_features.title: Static asset hygiene for generated UI images
existing_features.description: UI components consistently reference generated images under /assets/generated/... intended to be served from frontend/public/assets/generated under stable filenames to avoid runtime 404s.

existing_features.title: Internet Identity authentication provider (DFINITY)
existing_features.description: Provides a React Context managing AuthClient initialization, loading persisted identity, login/logout actions, and derived status flags/errors for consumption by UI components.

existing_features.title: Identity-aware canister actor hook (React Query)
existing_features.description: Creates and caches an ICP backend actor keyed by the current principal; returns an anonymous actor when unauthenticated and invalidates/refetches other queries when the actor changes.

existing_features.title: Backend canister scaffold (Motoko stub)
existing_features.description: Includes an empty Motoko actor (backend/main.mo) as a placeholder for future backend methods.

existing_features.title: No-backend query placeholder hook module
existing_features.description: Contains an intentionally empty useQueries module indicating the Valentine UI currently does not require backend queries and is locally state-driven.

existing_features.title: Generate a new cartoon kitty illustration (with a love/heart symbol) based on the uploaded reference image (IMG_2195-2.jpeg), and use it as the primary kitty illustration on the proposal/home screen (replace the currently referenced /assets/generated/proposal-kitty.jpeg usage in the UI).

Ensure all UI-referenced generated static assets used by the proposal/home screen exist under frontend/public/assets/generated and that the app does not reference missing filenames (including the primary kitty asset and any background/pattern assets).

Fix the “No” button behavior so it persists at all times on all devices (especially mobile): it must never disappear/vanish due to positioning, container bounds, or input-mode differences (mouse vs touch). Maintain the evasive behavior while ensuring the button remains visible and interactable.

Update the teasing message popups so that each click on “No” spawns a random teasing message at a random position on the screen, and the message visibly “hovers/moves around” after appearing. Each “No” click must create a new popup (random message and random starting position) while keeping the “No” button present.

Improve the proposal/home screen background to be more classy and aesthetic while staying Valentine-themed; update styling so the background feels intentional and premium (e.g., refined gradients, subtle texture/pattern, and consistent contrast with the card/content).

new_feature_requests.summary: Generate and insert a new cartoon kitty-with-love illustration based on the provided reference (do not use external/uploaded photo); ensure it renders on the home/proposal screen
Update background to be more classy/aesthetic (improve overall visual styling of home/proposal screen)
Ensure the “No” button persists at all times across devices (fix mobile disappearing/vanishing); keep evasion behavior on proximity without removing the button

On each “No” click, show a random teasing message that spawns at a random screen position and can animate/move around; optionally show teasing text above/near the moving No button while keeping/returning the “No” label

architectural_notes: React SPA using functional components and hooks; App.tsx holds the primary UI state machine (proposal vs success) and interaction state (no-click count, evasive button position, popup list).
Visual effects are encapsulated as components (FloatingHearts, Fireworks) and driven by CSS keyframes + small amounts of JS (randomized particles, timers/intervals).
TailwindCSS is used with OKLCH CSS-variable tokens (light/dark) and custom utility animations defined in global CSS; Tailwind config extends a Valentine palette and glow shadow.
Provider-based infrastructure is bootstrapped in main.tsx (QueryClientProvider + InternetIdentityProvider) even though the main page currently uses only local state.
Internet Identity authentication is implemented via a React Context wrapper around @dfinity/auth-client with identity persistence and status flags.
Canister access is abstracted behind a useActor hook that creates/caches an actor keyed by the current principal via @tanstack/react-query; actor changes invalidate/refetch other queries.
Static images are served from the frontend public path under /assets/generated/... and referenced directly from components.
known_issues: backend/main.mo defines an empty actor (no methods), so the ICP actor/auth scaffolding cannot perform meaningful backend calls yet.

Two different global CSS files exist (frontend/index.css and frontend/src/index.css) with different token sets; this duplication can cause confusion about which styling is actually applied (main.tsx imports src/index.css).

The UI references multiple static assets under /assets/generated/... (e.g., floating-hearts-pattern.dim_1024x768.png, proposal-kitty.jpeg, kitty-love.dim_512x512.png); these files must exist in frontend/public for deployments to avoid broken image requests (assets not visible in provided file list).

The “No” button switches to absolute positioning after the first click; if noButtonPosition hasn’t been updated yet, it may momentarily jump to (0,0) within the container until a proximity move occurs.
DEFAULT_IDENTITY_PROVIDER comes from process.env.II_URL; if missing/misconfigured, Internet Identity login will fail at runtime.
useActor invalidates and refetches all non-actor queries when the actor changes; in a larger app this could cause unnecessary refetch storms.
useQueries.ts is an intentionally empty placeholder; importing query hooks from it would be a dead end unless implemented later.
Cartoon kitty illustration is not rendering on the home/proposal screen (broken/missing asset or incorrect reference).
On mobile, the “No” button can disappear/vanish without a click; it must persist across interactions.
